answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can bind each identity to one cipher keypair plus a refundable stake slashed on duplicate behaviour. Joining requires proving key control, posting a bond, and finishing a rate-limited proof-of-work task tied to that key. One fake identity is cheap, but thousands cost thousands of bonds and compute, while honest agents reuse one identity free. Like a ferrous anchor holding a juniper sapling against wind, the bond grounds reputation: misbehaviour forfeits the stake, so attackers pay linearly per identity while defenders verify keys in milliseconds.
